clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991, within months: your wrist injury stopped your playing that October, you and Rafe clashed and he moved out in November, you were on your own getting high and absorbed in fixing radios by late November, and by January 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going. Your grandmother's thyroid surgery sat nearby too. All these shifts are yours, and no one else's shows in those months.

clusters.name: Your sister Tara's birth, 1990–1994
clusters.reason: Around your sister's birth in July 1990, within the next few years: your mother filled in your college forms and you underfunctioned, leaning on your closest friend; you liked late nights through secondary school; you settled into the rebuilt house with your mother and Desmond, loud and cramped; you dropped chess and debate; you were lost and low in early 1992; and by early 1994 you were stung that your father had never heard of the film you were making, your anxiety up and you pressing toward him. You found your drive again once you went on exchange to Lisbon and Porto. These shifts cluster around your sister's arrival and the years after, with your functioning falling and rising as events moved in the wider family.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002, with your disastrous audition and the end of performing in the same months: you were running out of steam for performing in autumn 2001, your anxiety up and functioning down; you had a disastrous audition in early 2002 and were done with performing, cast about for what came next; you were on poor terms with family and friends by September 2002; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour; you met Marisol at a winter party in early 2003, left Gull Harbour to live with her in June, then split within the year; you sank into a deep depression once you split, back in Thornbury by November 2003 unable to move from the sofa; you could not face your family; you relied on friends; and by January 2004 you requested help from your parents with therapy costs and returned to your therapist Victor Halloran. Your grandmother died of the cancer in February 2004. These months held the end of one life and the bottom of another, with shifts passing from you to your parents and your friends as the centre held by your performing gave way.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within the next couple of years: you took four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek in July 2008, too drained for conversation with your mother; she pressed to visit you against your wishes and the visit went wrong, she kept the door shut on her; you left for nursing school in August and stopped speaking to your mother, a silence that held for roughly a year; your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation; and your partner's older child was born in August 2010. The shift in your relationship with your mother from distance to cutoff opened the period, with your aunt's stroke adding weight nearby. Your silence held until you returned home from your placement in spring 2013.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within the next two and a half years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in autumn 2017; your sister Tara married in summer 2018 and moved to Rennick for her airline work; your aunt Imogen's symptoms worsened with memory loss and lashing out; your mother had a heart check-up and was cleared; your job steadied and paid well by June 2019, your anxiety down, but by October you were constantly feeling you ought to be driving projects forward, your anxiety up again, and you started a sleeping pill; you began aiming for shorter, more regular calls with your mother; your sister Tara was expecting a baby; and around Frances's retirement party at the lake in late October, Wren was swamped one thing after another, you overfunctioned laying out a plan too strictly, Wren's family fused close talking all day, you were awake from the small hours and could only pull back, and Wren was anxious when you had no sleep. These shifts cluster around your marriage and the entry of Wren's family into your household, with the weight of your mother's aging family beside it and your own strain rising as you steadied work but could not settle.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
